Always Show Control Center listing copy vs Lock Screen security engineering — two different jobs

Teams assume lock-screen Control Center compatibility covers storefront language. iOS Settings and App Store Connect actually separate them:

  • Always Show Control Center on the device — the Allow Access When Locked toggle under Settings → Face ID & Passcode or Touch ID & Passcode → Control Center. When on, buyers swipe down from the top-right corner (Face ID models) or up from the bottom (Home button models) to open Control Center while the phone stays locked. System security UI — outside AppLocale scope.
  • Lock-screen quick toggles inside Control Center — Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Airplane Mode, Focus, flashlight tile, camera shortcut, and third-party iOS 18+ Controls reachable after the swipe. Some actions still require Face ID or passcode when iOS treats them as sensitive — listing copy should match what your screenshots actually show.
  • Always Show Control Center marketing on the product page — description paragraphs, subtitle positioning, keywords, promotional text, and screenshot overlays that tell buyers your app pairs with lock-screen Control Center access, teaches the Allow Access When Locked path, or shows quick toggles without unlocking. Connect text fields — this page.

  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and screenshot caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of how strongly your US listing markets Always Show Control Center.

An app that references lock-screen Control Center workflows in onboarding and a localized China listing are both valuable — neither replaces the other.
